newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog to fix MGAM payout this month.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog to fix MGAM payout this month.

text.p: UK fund management regulator IMRO said on Monday it hoped this month to agree a method for calculating compensation due to investors hurt by a crisis in September at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).

The regulator dismissed as "pure speculation" a report in the Guardian newspaper over the weekend claiming that the parent of MGAM, Germany's Deutsche Bank, would have to repatriate 200 million stg to make good investors' losses.
"Until we actually complete assessing and agree what the method of calculation should be, we won't be able to assess what the amount of compensation should be," said a spokeswoman.

She said that IMRO hoped to agree on a method of calculation before the end of this year and that investors would receive compensation in the first quarter of next year. The regulator said that addressing the issue of compensation was its chief priority. Any disciplinary action against MGAM would occur early next year and any action against individuals would probably follow that.

Deutsche has injected 180 million stg into MGAM after three of the unit's European funds had to be temporarily suspended in September, pending an investigation into the valuation of unlisted speculative stocks they contained.

The bank, Germany's largest, has also dismissed the fund manager at the centre of the crisis, Peter Young, and four more senior managers. The funds concerned, held by some 90,000 retail investors, resumed trading after Deutsche's cash injection.
